Tutorial 6: Identifying a Sample

Beatriz M. Meriño

2026-10-16

Source: vignettes/tutorial-6-cactus-barcoding-identification.Rmd
tutorial-6-cactus-barcoding-identification.Rmd

Abstract

Tutorial 5 builds the reference library of 15 loci and validates it. This tutorial uses that library to identify samples: one worked example for each kind of input the package accepts, all of them public records that are not in the library, so that each answer is what a user would get for a sample of their own.

Each example has three parts:

  1. Download. The record is fetched from its public source (GenBank, NCBI Assembly or ENA) into a folder examples/.
  2. Identification. The function of the package is called with the path of the file, as for any sample.
  3. Result. The answer per locus, drawn with plot_barcoding_identification(), one line of reading, and a link to the full HTML report.

The reports on the website were written from the tables of the identification runs, made before the version number of the package was set to 0.5.0: their provenance table gives 0.4.5.9000, the number the package carried when the samples were identified, and their footer gives 0.5.0, the version that wrote the page.

The script tutorial-6-cactus-barcoding-identification.R runs all of it from the tutorial folder:

file.edit(system.file("scripts", "tutorial-6-cactus-barcoding-identification.R", package = "PhyloCactus"))

The figures on this page are drawn from the answer tables of these examples, distributed with the package in inst/extdata; the script draws the same figures from your own run.

Before You Start

  • The library of Tutorial 5, in the same tutorial folder: 11_barcoding/4_library/ (step 4), 11_barcoding/9_threshold/ (step 9) and 11_barcoding/11_metrics/ (step 10).
  • rentrez, for the GenBank downloads.
  • minimap2 and samtools for the assembly, fastp and GetOrganelle (with its seed databases embplant_pt and embplant_nr) for the reads. If they live in a conda environment, activate it in the terminal before starting R there.

Reading an Answer

Every locus of the library is looked for in the sample and answered on its own, in one of three states:

  • State 1, species. IdTaxa names a species and its species confidence reaches the species threshold of the locus (set in step 9 of Tutorial 5 from the validation queries whose species was absent from the library).
  • State 2, genus. The genus confidence reaches 60. A species reached under the species threshold is kept as an alternative, never assigned, with reason below_species_threshold. rbcL answers at genus rank only in this version (reason genus_only_locus, argument genus_only_loci): on the library of this version its species answers were right in 11 of 34.
  • State 3, no answer, with its reason: no_overlap (the locus is not in the sample), short_overlap, or low_confidence.

Loci are never combined into one verdict. When several loci answer, the report shows whether they agree; when they name different taxa, the answer of the sample is a conflict. A region identical to library sequences is reported in identical_to_library, so that the records behind a confident answer can be checked.

Example 1. One Sanger Record

LT745702.1, matK of Pseudorhipsalis amazonica subsp. panamensis. The record is named at subspecies rank, so the mining of Tutorial 1 left it out; the library holds its binomial.

# Download (GenBank, 1 record)
writeLines(rentrez::entrez_fetch("nuccore", id = "LT745702.1", rettype = "gb", retmode = "text"),
           "examples/LT745702.1.gb")
identify_barcoding_query("examples/LT745702.1.gb", run_name = "LT745702.1")

Figure 1. Answer of the Sanger record LT745702.1. IdTaxa confidence of each locus found, at genus rank (striped bar) and species rank (solid bar), coloured by state (dark blue, species; light blue, genus; grey, no answer), with the threshold as a dashed line; below, the species of the named genus in the library and their sequences per locus.

Reading. matK names the genus Pseudorhipsalis. IdTaxa reached the right species, P. amazonica, with a species confidence of 61.6, under the species threshold of matK (66.9): the species is listed as an alternative (below_species_threshold), not assigned. trnQ-rps16 overlaps too little (short_overlap). Full report.

Example 2. A Specimen of Unknown Species

PZ714536.1, matK of Opuntia sp., published after the mining of Tutorial 1.

writeLines(rentrez::entrez_fetch("nuccore", id = "PZ714536.1", rettype = "gb", retmode = "text"),
           "examples/PZ714536.1.gb")
identify_barcoding_query("examples/PZ714536.1.gb", run_name = "PZ714536.1")

Figure 2. Answer of the Sanger record PZ714536.1 (Opuntia sp.). IdTaxa confidence of each locus found, at genus rank (striped bar) and species rank (solid bar), coloured by state (dark blue, species; light blue, genus; grey, no answer), with the threshold as a dashed line; below, the species of the named genus in the library and their sequences per locus.

Reading. Opuntia at genus rank (genus confidence 79.2). The region is identical to 17 library records of several species of Opuntia, so no species can be told apart at this locus. Full report.

Example 3. One Specimen, Four Loci

Coryphantha elephantidens subsp. bumamma, voucher Vázquez 2628: OK340410.1, OK340349.1, OK340287.1, OK340224.1. Given with sample =, the four records are one sample, read together in one report.

writeLines(rentrez::entrez_fetch("nuccore", id = c("OK340410.1", "OK340349.1", "OK340287.1", "OK340224.1"),
                                 rettype = "gb", retmode = "text"), "examples/OK340410.1_specimen.gb")
identify_barcoding_query("examples/OK340410.1_specimen.gb", sample = "Coryphantha_elephantidens_bumamma",
                         run_name = "OK340410.1")

Figure 3. Answer of the specimen of Coryphantha elephantidens subsp. bumamma (four loci). IdTaxa confidence of each locus found, at genus rank (striped bar) and species rank (solid bar), coloured by state (dark blue, species; light blue, genus; grey, no answer), with the threshold as a dashed line; below, the species of the named genus in the library and their sequences per locus.

Reading. matK and rbcL name Coryphantha; rpL16 and psbA-trnH give no answer (low confidence). The two loci that answer agree, and the sample is answered at genus rank. Full report.

Example 4. One Specimen, Four Loci, and a Wrong Species

Xiquexique gounellei: OP189074.1, OP188885.1, OP188764.1, OP187233.1.

writeLines(rentrez::entrez_fetch("nuccore", id = c("OP189074.1", "OP188885.1", "OP188764.1", "OP187233.1"),
                                 rettype = "gb", retmode = "text"), "examples/OP189074.1_specimen.gb")
identify_barcoding_query("examples/OP189074.1_specimen.gb", sample = "Xiquexique_gounellei", run_name = "OP189074.1")

Figure 4. Answer of the specimen of Xiquexique gounellei (four loci). IdTaxa confidence of each locus found, at genus rank (striped bar) and species rank (solid bar), coloured by state (dark blue, species; light blue, genus; grey, no answer), with the threshold as a dashed line; below, the species of the named genus in the library and their sequences per locus.

Reading. ITS names Xiquexique frewenii with a species confidence of 62.5, just over its species threshold (60.9); the other three loci give no answer. A species named by one locus, close to its threshold, with every other locus silent, is the pattern of most wrong species of this version: read it as the genus until another locus agrees. Full report.

Example 5. A GenBank Plastome Named to Species

MN517611.1, the plastome of Mammillaria zephyranthoides. A GenBank flat file is read as such; each locus is cropped from the plastome.

writeLines(rentrez::entrez_fetch("nuccore", id = "MN517611.1", rettype = "gb", retmode = "text"),
           "examples/MN517611.1.gb")
identify_barcoding_query("examples/MN517611.1.gb", run_name = "MN517611.1")

Figure 5. Answer of the plastome MN517611.1. IdTaxa confidence of each locus found, at genus rank (striped bar) and species rank (solid bar), coloured by state (dark blue, species; light blue, genus; grey, no answer), with the threshold as a dashed line; below, the species of the named genus in the library and their sequences per locus.

Reading. matK names Mammillaria zephyranthoides (82.8 against 66.9), among the species of Mammillaria of its library; the other loci found give no answer. Full report.

Example 6. A GenBank Plastome Named as Another Species

MT387452.1, the plastome of Rhipsalis teres.

writeLines(rentrez::entrez_fetch("nuccore", id = "MT387452.1", rettype = "gb", retmode = "text"),
           "examples/MT387452.1.gb")
identify_barcoding_query("examples/MT387452.1.gb", run_name = "MT387452.1")

Figure 6. Answer of the plastome MT387452.1. IdTaxa confidence of each locus found, at genus rank (striped bar) and species rank (solid bar), coloured by state (dark blue, species; light blue, genus; grey, no answer), with the threshold as a dashed line; below, the species of the named genus in the library and their sequences per locus.

Reading. matK names Lepismium lumbricoides (81.2 against 66.9): the region is identical to FN669720.1, a record under that name (identical_to_library). An identical sequence under another name, a misidentified voucher or a haplotype shared across genera, yields a confident wrong answer; the report lists the record so that it can be checked. Full report.

Example 7. Several Samples at Once

A sample sheet has one row per sample: sample_id, input_type (a row of the matrix of accepted inputs, barcoding_accepted_inputs.csv), file_1, and optionally file_2, declared_species and voucher. Each sample is routed to its function and gets its report; one index table gathers them.

sheet <- data.frame(sample_id = c("LT745702.1", "PZ714536.1", "MN517611.1"),
                    input_type = "genbank",
                    file_1 = c("examples/LT745702.1.gb", "examples/PZ714536.1.gb", "examples/MN517611.1.gb"),
                    declared_species = c("Pseudorhipsalis amazonica", "", "Mammillaria zephyranthoides"))
utils::write.csv(sheet, "examples/samples.csv", row.names = FALSE)
identify_barcoding_samples("examples/samples.csv")

The index, 11_barcoding/10_identify/samples/TABLE_barcoding_samples_index.csv, compares each answer with the declared species: species agrees, genus agrees, disagrees, not assigned, or not declared when the sheet gives none. The three samples are the records of Examples 1, 2 and 5, and their answers per locus are the figures of those examples; what the sheet adds is the index:

Table 1. Index of the sample sheet of Example 7: loci found, rows per state, the genera and species named, and the answer against the declared species.
Sample Loci found State 1 State 2 State 3 Genera named Species named Declared species Answer vs declared
LT745702.1 2 0 1 1 Pseudorhipsalis Pseudorhipsalis amazonica genus agrees
PZ714536.1 1 0 1 0 Opuntia not declared
MN517611.1 12 1 0 11 Mammillaria Mammillaria zephyranthoides Mammillaria zephyranthoides species agrees

Reading. LT745702.1 names the genus Pseudorhipsalis and its declared species is not reached (genus agrees). PZ714536.1 names Opuntia and declares no species (not declared). MN517611.1 names Mammillaria zephyranthoides at one of its 12 loci found (species agrees). The sheet gives no voucher, so voucher_missing is TRUE in the three rows: a sample without a voucher is identified and flagged, since the leakage rule per specimen cannot be applied to it (its report says so).

Example 8. A Genome Assembly

GCA_024363205.1, Cereus fernambucensis (NCBI Assembly, about 0.9 Gb). The loci of the library are mapped onto the assembly with minimap2 and cut with samtools.

s <- rentrez::entrez_summary("assembly", rentrez::entrez_search("assembly", "GCA_024363205.1[Assembly Accession]")$ids[1])
ftp <- sub("^ftp://", "https://", s$ftppath_genbank)   # https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/024/363/205/...
asm <- file.path("examples", paste0(basename(ftp), "_genomic.fna.gz"))
utils::download.file(paste0(ftp, "/", basename(ftp), "_genomic.fna.gz"), asm, mode = "wb")
identify_barcoding_assembly(asm, run_name = "GCA_024363205.1")

Figure 7. Answer of the assembly GCA_024363205.1. IdTaxa confidence of each locus found, at genus rank (striped bar) and species rank (solid bar), coloured by state (dark blue, species; light blue, genus; grey, no answer), with the threshold as a dashed line; below, the species of the named genus in the library and their sequences per locus.

Reading. Cereus at genus rank from pepC_like (its best species at 61.5, under the species threshold of 78.8) and phyC; 12 other loci give no answer. rpl32-trnL hits two scaffolds with a low mapping quality, which the package reports; the best hit is kept. Full report.

Example 9. Paired Illumina Reads

SRR26398994, a genome skim of Opuntia comonduensis (ENA, about 0.56 GB). The plastome and the nuclear ribosomal DNA are assembled with fastp and GetOrganelle, then identified locus by locus. The species is not in the library.

ena <- utils::read.delim(paste0("https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=SRR26398994",
                                "&result=read_run&fields=fastq_ftp,fastq_md5&format=tsv"), colClasses = "character")
urls <- paste0("https://", strsplit(ena$fastq_ftp, ";")[[1]])
fq <- file.path("examples", basename(urls))
for (k in 1:2) utils::download.file(urls[k], fq[k], mode = "wb")
stopifnot(unname(tools::md5sum(fq)) == strsplit(ena$fastq_md5, ";")[[1]])
identify_barcoding_reads(fq[1], fq[2], run_name = "SRR26398994", threads = 4)

Figure 8. Answer of the reads SRR26398994. IdTaxa confidence of each locus found, at genus rank (striped bar) and species rank (solid bar), coloured by state (dark blue, species; light blue, genus; grey, no answer), with the threshold as a dashed line; below, the species of the named genus in the library and their sequences per locus.

Reading. Opuntia at genus rank from ndhF-rpl32; the other ten loci found give no answer. For a species absent from the library, the genus is the right answer. Full report.

The Examples Side by Side

Figure 9. The answers of the eight examples with a figure, side by side: one row per example and one column per locus found, coloured by state; a cross marks a locus named at genus rank only (genus_only_locus).

A plastome or an assembly holds most loci of the library, a Sanger record one; yet in these examples the answer rests on one or two loci in every case, and most loci found give no answer.

How Well This Version Identifies

The rates below were measured with the library of this version, built from GenBank alone on 2026-10-13, with the species thresholds of step 9 and rbcL at genus rank only. They belong to this library: as GenBank enriches it, they are measured again and are expected to change.

Outcomes, in the order species correct / genus correct / no answer / conflict / wrong species / wrong genus (number of queries). A species is “present” when the library holds it once the records of the query’s own specimen are set aside.

Input Unit Species present Species absent
One Sanger record of the library, own specimen set aside locus 148 / 402 / 1738 / n.a. / 14 / 2 (2304) 0 / 252 / 2173 / n.a. / 45 / 37 (2507)
Sanger records of one GenBank specimen specimen 6 / 52 / 99 / 0 / 1 / 0 (158) 0 / 22 / 19 / 0 / 1 / 0 (42)
GenBank plastome plastome 3 / 51 / 26 / 1 / 1 / 11 (93) 0 / 2 / 0 / 1 / 0 / 1 (4)
Illumina reads (genome skims) run 1 / 2 / 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 (4) 0 / 1 / 2 / 0 / 0 / 0 (3)

Records from outside the library are a harder query than library records with their own specimen set aside. Of 94 Sanger records from outside the library (named at subspecies or variety, or with no species name, so left out of the mining), identified one by one, none was named at species rank: 48 were answered at the right genus and 46 not at all (5 with no locus found). Where IdTaxa reached the right species, it did so under the species threshold (below_species_threshold), as in example 1. Of 23 specimens with several of these records, 17 were answered at the right genus, 5 not at all, and 1 at a wrong species (example 4).

The genus is the answer to expect from this version. A species is named rarely, mostly from matK and from plastomes; abstention is the most common answer, and a wrong species is rare but possible.

Limitations

  • Coverage of the library. A sample of a species absent from a locus library can only be named as something else at that locus, or not at all. The library holds part of the accepted species of the checklist of Korotkova et al. (2021), unevenly across loci; Tutorial 5 draws its taxonomic coverage.
  • Shared sequences. Identical sequences under different names (shared haplotypes, misidentified vouchers) give confident wrong answers; identical_to_library names them.
  • Thresholds. The species thresholds come from the validation of the library; a species named close to its threshold by one locus deserves the caution of example 4.

References

  • Korotkova et al. 2021. Cactaceae at Caryophyllales.org - A dynamic online species-level taxonomic backbone for the family. Willdenowia, 51(2), 251–270. https://doi.org/10.3372/wi.51.51208
  • Murali et al. 2018. IDTAXA: a novel approach for accurate taxonomic classification of microbiome sequences. Microbiome, 6. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40168-018-0521-5
